messages.subject: Local Package Installation Help
parts:

> packrat::install_local('reshape2_1.4.tar.gz')

  --library="C:/Users/ericad/Documents/R working/WORK  \
  Packages/PACKRATMYPKG/packrat/lib/x86_64-w64-mingw32/3.1.2" --install-tests 

In other cases it does not work (even when i installed the package dependencies first):

> packrat::install_local('rgdal_0.9-1.tar.gz')
Installing package from '~/R/rgdal_0.9-1.tar.gz'

"C:/PROGRA~1/R/R-31~1.2/bin/x64/R" --vanilla CMD build "C:\Users\ericad\AppData\Local\Temp\RtmpaYuHoL\rgdal" --no-manual  \
  --no-resave-data 

Error: Command failed (1)

The command failed with output:
* checking for file 'C:\Users\ericad\AppData\Local\Temp\RtmpaYuHoL\rgdal/DESCRIPTION' ... OK
* preparing 'rgdal':
* checking DESCRIPTION meta-information ... OK
* cleaning src

Warning: running command '"C:/PROGRA~1/R/R-31~1.2/bin/x64/Rcmd.exe" INSTALL -l "C:\Users\ericad\AppData\Local\Temp\RtmpgD1wZp\Rinstf80251c60b1" --no-multiarch "C:/Users/ericad/AppData/Local/Temp/RtmpgD1wZp/Rbuildf8055875623/rgdal"' had status 1
      -----------------------------------
* installing *source* package 'rgdal' ...
file 'src/RGDAL.def' is missing
cp: cannot stat `/share/proj': No such file or directory
cp: cannot stat `/share/gdal': No such file or directory
Warning: running command 'sh ./configure.win' had status 1
ERROR: configuration failed for package 'rgdal'
* removing 'C:/Users/ericad/AppData/Local/Temp/RtmpgD1wZp/Rinstf80251c60b1/rgdal'

ERROR: package

What is going on?  I really need to use packrat in this case because this script needs data.table v. 1.9.4 but all of the other scripts that i have written need data.table 1.9.2.  If i install 1.9.4 i will not be able to run any of my other scripts (years worth of work).  Below is my session info.

messages.author: ab0d2be2ea8dabe8
messages.subject: Re: Local Package Installation Help
parts:
Hi Erica,

Some packages, like `rgdal`, require a lot of external dependencies in order to be able to install from source -- for `rgdal`, I would suggest installing the latest binary version from CRAN.

You should, however, be able to install `data.table` from sources fairly easily, as long as you have the appropriate version of `Rtools` (http://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/) installed. Your success in installing `reshape2` suggests it is already available.

Is it possible that you could use packrat, but instead use the latest CRAN binary version of `rgdal` rather than an older 'installed from source' version? I believe that would resolve your problems.

Finally -- the ability of packrat to manage only _a subset of_ dependencies is currently a bit of a pain point. That is, in your case, you want to stay tied to a particular version of `data.table`, but are probably fine with installing latest CRAN versions of other packages -- does that sound correct? This is something we want to make easier to do with packrat, but have not yet done.

Thanks,
Kevin

Kevin-

thanks for the quick response.  i will try using the newest version of rgdal in packrat with my code and see if that works.  The only reason i thought it might be an issue is that the code doesn't work properly in packrat but does in non-packrat mode with my user library.  so i was trying to get all of the packages in packrat to be the same as in my user library (except data.table).  i will try to get my packrat library as close to my user library as i can and hopefully that will work.  Is there any way that i could import directly from my user library (i.e., the folders that get produced after i install a package from the CRAN) into my packrat library?  Or is there a way that i could install rgdal from the CRAN in packrat mode so that all the dependencies get installed properly and then overwrite just rgdal with an older version?

-erica-
